core_obligations: Reduce the base: localize and then complete to assume the base is a Noetherian local Cohen-Macaulay ring possessing a dualizing complex, and reduce further to a maximal ideal of the source lying over the maximal ideal of the base (proof lines 5366-5396)

Rewrite the relative complex: write the base dualizing complex as a single module in degree minus the dimension and express the relative complex as the internal hom of its tensor with the source into the shriek of the base complex (proof lines 5399-5408)

Vanishing: the dimension formula bounds the dimension of the local source by the dimension plus the transcendence degree bound, so the localized shriek is a normalized dualizing complex whose cohomology is confined to an interval, and the tensor factor lives in low degrees, which gives the asserted vanishing (proof lines 5409-5420)

The S2 statement: the lowest surviving cohomology module is the internal hom of a module over the base into the lowest cohomology of the shriek, and since that module is S2 the cited statement shows the internal hom is S2 (proof lines 5421-5429)
proof_roadmap: (1) the base may be localized and then completed (the completion stays Cohen-Macaulay) and one may pass to a local base with a dualizing complex, so assume R is local Cohen-Macaulay with a dualizing complex.
(2) take omega_R normalized, omega_R^bullet = omega_R[d], and omega_A^bullet = phi^!(omega_R^bullet); the relative complex is RHom_A(omega_R[d] tensor^L_R A, omega_A^bullet).

(3) by the dimension formula dim(A_m) <= d + r, and by the shriek normalization the localized omega_A^bullet is a normalized dualizing complex, so its cohomology sits in [-d-r, 0]; the tensor factor lives in degrees <= -d, which gives the vanishing range.

(4) the lowest cohomology is Hom_A(omega_R tensor_R A, H^{-d-r}(omega_A^bullet))_m and H^{-d-r}(omega_A^bullet)_m is S2, so the internal hom into an S2 module is S2 by the cited More on Algebra statement.
difficulty_reason: The counted statement gives, for a finite type map of Noetherian rings over a Cohen-Macaulay local base, a lower bound on the degrees in which the relative dualizing complex can be nonzero in terms of the transcendence degree of the fibres, and shows that the lowest surviving cohomology module is S2 (author lemma at source lines 5348-5363, label lemma-relative-dualizing-CM-vanishing). The proof (source lines 5365-5430) reduces to a local Cohen-Macaulay base by localization and completion, rewrites the relative complex through a normalized dualizing complex of the base, bounds the dimension of the localized source by the dimension formula, reads the vanishing range off the degree confinement statement, and obtains the S2 statement from the S2 property of the lowest cohomology of the normalized shriek (proof lines 5409-5429). The reduction to the normalized local situation is the substance. H3.
